name: Zimri
charge: Conspiring against his master Elah as he drank himself drunk; slaying all the house of Baasha
summary: Captain of half the chariots, Zimri killed his king in a steward's house and took the throne. Seven days later the army chose Omri, Tirzah was taken, and Zimri burned the king's house over his own head. His name became a byword: Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?
offense: Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots. While the king drank himself drunk in the house of his steward Arza, Zimri conspired, struck him, and reigned in his stead (1 Kings 16:8-10). Military office gave him access that he turned against his master. He then destroyed Baasha's house, sparing neither kinsfolk nor friends. The overthrow fulfilled the word spoken through Jehu against Baasha and Elah, but Zimri also walked in Jeroboam's sin (1 Kings 16:11-13, 19). His success in removing the old house did not establish a righteous one. The change was in the man holding the palace, not in the kingdom's obedience. Baasha had repeated Jeroboam's course after destroying his descendants; Zimri repeated it after destroying Baasha's. The accumulated examples of judgment did not persuade the next claimant to forsake the sin beneath them.
judgment: The army encamped against Gibbethon heard that Zimri had conspired and slain the king. It made Omri, captain of the host, king that day. Omri and Israel went up from the camp and besieged Tirzah (1 Kings 16:15-17). Holding the palace did not mean holding the allegiance of the army. When Zimri saw that the city was taken, he went into the palace, burned the king's house over himself, and died. His reign lasted seven days (1 Kings 16:15, 18). The place seized as the seat of his advancement became the place of his death. The account names his sins and treason, not merely Omri's greater force (1 Kings 16:19-20). Years later Jezebel invoked his name against Jehu: had Zimri peace, who slew his master (2 Kings 9:31)? His short reign remained a warning that the killing of a king did not secure the killer's future. The advantage gained through conspiracy was consumed before it could become an enduring house.

verses.text: In the twenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasha to reign over Israel in Tirzah, two years.
And his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him, as he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza steward of his house in Tirzah.
And Zimri went in and smote him, and killed him, in the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his stead.

And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he slew all the house of Baasha: he left him not one that pisseth against a wall, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.
Thus did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,
For all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, by which they sinned, and by which they made Israel to sin, in provoking the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
In the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah did Zimri reign seven days in Tirzah. And the people were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
And the people that were encamped heard say, Zimri hath conspired, and hath also slain the king: wherefore all Israel made Omri, the captain of the host, king over Israel that day in the camp.
And Omri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besieged Tirzah.
And it came to pass, when Zimri saw that the city was taken, that he went into the palace of the king’s house, and burnt the king’s house over him with fire, and died,
For his sins which he sinned in doing evil in the sight of the Lord, in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin which he did, to make Israel to sin.
Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and his treason that he wrought, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And as Jehu entered in at the gate, she said, Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?
A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.

entries.commentary: The word of the Most High comes to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, because though he was exalted out of the dust and made prince over Israel, he walked in the way of Jeroboam and made Israel sin. Therefore the Most High will make his house like the house of Jeroboam, and those who die in the city the dogs will eat and those in the field the fowls will eat. The same judgment falls because the same sin is repeated, just as descendants keep the pattern of their fathers though they saw the ruin it brought.

Elah son of Baasha reigns two years, and his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspires against him while he is drunk in a steward's house and kills him. Zimri, on taking the throne, slays all the house of Baasha, leaving not one male, according to the word spoken by Jehu against Baasha. All of it comes for the sins of Baasha and Elah, who provoked the Most High to anger with their vanities. -

Zimri reigns only seven days in Tirzah. When the people encamped against Gibbethon hear he has slain the king, they make Omri, captain of the host, king over Israel. Omri and Israel go up and besiege Tirzah, and when Zimri sees the city taken, he burns the king's house over himself and dies. His death comes for his sins in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and his treason is recorded, treason being punishable by death in that time.

Israel is divided: half follow Tibni son of Ginath and half follow Omri, but Omri's followers prevail, Tibni dies, and Omri reigns. Omri buys the hill Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, builds the city, and names it after Shemer. Omri does worse than all before him, walking in the way of Jeroboam, then sleeps with his fathers, and Ahab his son reigns in his place.

Ahab son of Omri reigns twenty-two years in Samaria and does evil above all that were before him. As if walking in Jeroboam's sins were a light thing, he takes Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians to wife and serves and worships Baal, rearing an altar and a grove, provoking the Most High more than all the kings before him. This mirrors Solomon, who followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and the marrying outside the people that the law forbids because it turns the heart to other gods. In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilds Jericho, laying its foundation in his firstborn Abiram and setting up its gates in his youngest Segub, according to the word spoken by Joshua. -

Elisha sends one of the children of the prophets to Ramoth-gilead to anoint Jehu king over Israel, pour the oil on his head, and flee. Jehu is charged to smite the house of Ahab to avenge the blood of the prophets and of the servants of the Most High shed at the hand of Jezebel, whose work was to kill the prophets while weak Ahab let it continue. The word declares the whole house of Ahab shall perish, and the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel with none to bury her.

Jehu's fellow captains ask why the mad fellow came, and when he tells them the prophet anointed him king, they hasten to put their garments under him and blow the trumpets, proclaiming Jehu king. Jehu conspires against Jehoram and charges that none escape the city to carry the news to Jezreel. He rides toward Jezreel where Jehoram lay wounded, and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see him.

A watchman spies Jehu's company, and two horsemen sent to ask if it is peace are each told to turn behind him and do not return, for the driving is furious like the driving of Jehu. Jehoram himself goes out and asks if it is peace, and Jehu answers that there can be no peace while the whoredoms and witchcrafts of his mother Jezebel are so many. Jehu draws his bow with full strength and smites Jehoram through the heart, then casts him into the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite according to the word of the Most High.

Ahaziah king of Judah flees but Jehu pursues and has him smitten in his chariot; he flees to Megiddo and dies there. His servants carry him to Jerusalem and bury him in the sepulchre of his fathers in the city of David.

Jezebel paints her face and tires her head, returning to her seductive ways as Jehu enters the gate. Jehu calls out for who is on his side, and two or three eunuchs look out. At Jehu's word they throw her down, her blood is sprinkled on the wall and the horses, and he treads her under foot. When they go to bury her they find only the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands, fulfilling the word spoken by Elijah that dogs would eat the flesh of Jezebel and her carcass would be as dung upon the field.

The wicked flee when no man pursues, but the righteous are bold as a lion. Peter and John were perceived as unlearned men, yet their boldness made men take knowledge that they had been with Christ, who taught as one having authority. We can be bold this same way by using the words of the Most High, which no one can gainsay. For the transgression of a land many are its princes, but by a man of understanding and knowledge its state shall be prolonged. That understanding and knowledge is the Most High's commandments; David told Solomon that keeping the commandments keeps a man on the throne of Israel. -

A poor man that oppresses the poor is like a sweeping rain that leaves no food. They that forsake the law praise the wicked, but such as keep the law contend with them, as we do daily in these scriptures. Evil men do not understand judgment, but they that seek the Most High understand all things. Better is the poor who walks uprightly than the perverse rich man.

Whoever keeps the law is a wise son, but a companion of riotous men shames his father. He that increases his substance by usury and unjust gain gathers it for one who will pity the poor. He that turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be an abomination, as [John 9](/bible/john/9) says the Most High does not hear sinners. -

Whoever causes the righteous to go astray in an evil way shall fall into his own pit, but the upright shall have good things. The rich man is wise in his own conceit, but the poor that has understanding searches him out. He that covers his sins shall not prosper, but whoever confesses and forsakes them shall have mercy. The Most High has mercy on those that forsake their sins; that is why we must repent, Israel. Happy is the man that fears always, but he that hardens his heart falls into mischief.

As a roaring lion and a raging bear, so is a wicked ruler over the people. The prince that lacks understanding is a great oppressor, but he that hates covetousness shall prolong his days. A man that does violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him. Whoever walks uprightly shall be saved, but he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once. Our people cannot say "I'm saved," for he that endures to the end shall be saved; [Ezekiel 18](/bible/ezekiel/18) shows that if your last act is evil, the Most High will not remember the good you did before.

He that tills his land shall have plenty of bread, but he that follows vain persons shall have poverty enough. Tilling the land is hard work, and the Most High says hate not laborious work; chasing vain persons means always being on some get-rich-quick scheme that does not work. A faithful man shall abound with blessings, but he that makes haste to be rich shall not be innocent. To have respect of persons is not good, for a piece of bread that man will transgress. He that hastens to be rich has an evil eye and does not consider that poverty will come; if you chase quick riches you care nothing for your victims.

He that rebukes a man shall afterward find more favor than he that flatters with the tongue. Whoever robs his father or mother and says it is no transgression is a companion of a destroyer. Think of the times, even as grown people, some went into a mother's purse or stole from a father; we must repent from these things, Israel. He that is of a proud heart stirs up strife, but he that puts his trust in the Most High shall be made fat.

He that trusts in his own heart is a fool, but whoever walks wisely shall be delivered. He that gives to the poor shall not lack, but he that hides his eyes shall have many a curse. Ecclesiasticus and the law say the same: do not turn your eye from the needy, and open your hand wide to your poor brother, for if he curses you in the bitterness of his soul his prayer is heard. [Sirach 12](/bible/sirach/12) says if you do good, know to whom you do it, and the law commands us to help our brothers who keep the commandments. When the wicked rise, men hide themselves, but when they perish the righteous increase. -
